definition: Existing or available in large quantities; overflowing or rich with resources.

mnemonic.story_en: The sea sent UND waves of fish to the shore, providing an ABUNDANT food supply for the villagers.
mnemonic.story_zh: 海浪（UND）不斷拍打上岸，帶來了「豐富的（ABUNDANT）」魚類資源。

example: The region is famous for its abundant natural resources, including timber and fresh water.

definition: To gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something gradually over a period of time.

mnemonic.story_en: Over the years, dust will CUMUL pile up and ACCUMULATE in corners if you do not clean them.
mnemonic.story_zh: 如果不打掃，灰塵就會在角落堆積（CUMUL）並「累積（ACCUMULATE）」起來。

example: He managed to accumulate a substantial fortune through wise stock investments.

definition: To accept or admit the existence or truth of something, or to express gratitude or recognition for something.
definition_zh: 承認；告知收到（信件等）；致謝

mnemonic.story_en: You must KNOW the truth first before you can ACKNOWLEDGE it in front of the public.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你必須先知道（KNOW）真相，才能在公眾面前「承認（ACKNOWLEDGE）」它。

example: The government refused to acknowledge that its policy had failed completely.

definition: To buy or obtain an asset or object, or to learn and develop a skill or habit.

mnemonic.story_en: Companies QUIR search for small startups to ACQUIRE new technology and expand their market.
mnemonic.story_zh: 大公司透過不斷尋找（QUIR）小新創公司來「收購（ACQUIRE）」新技術並擴大市場。

example: Children acquire their first language naturally without formal grammar lessons.

definition: Satisfactory or acceptable in quality or quantity; sufficient to meet a specific requirement.

mnemonic.story_en: When the supply is EQU equal to the demand, we have an ADEQUATE amount of resources.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當供應等同（EQU）於需求時，我們就有了「足夠的（ADEQUATE）」資源量。

example: The old laboratory lacks adequate equipment to carry out high-level chemical experiments.

definition: Next to or adjoining something else; having a common vertex or border.

mnemonic.story_en: The two rooms are JAC placed right next to each other, so they are ADJACENT.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩個房間被放（JAC）在彼此朝向（AD）的地方，代表它們是「鄰近的（ADJACENT）」。

example: We stayed in adjacent rooms, which made it very easy to coordinate our travel plans.

definition: To manage and organize the affairs of a business, organization, or government; also means to dispense or apply a remedy or drug.
definition_zh: 管理；執行；給予（藥物、懲罰）

mnemonic.story_en: The MINISTR officer is appointed to ADMINISTER the new public health programs.
mnemonic.story_zh: 政府委派官方執行人員（MINISTR）來「管理和執行（ADMINISTER）」新的公共衛生計劃。

example: The nurse is trained to administer emergency medicine when a patient suffers a stroke.

definition: To produce an effect on something; to make a difference to a person, thing, or situation.

mnemonic.story_en: Your continuous bad habits will FEC do damage and negatively AFFECT your long-term health.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你不好的習慣會產生作用（FEC）並進而「影響（AFFECT）」你的長期健康。

example: Extreme weather events significantly affect global crop production and food prices.

definition: A whole formed by combining several separate elements or numbers; a total or collective mass.

mnemonic.story_en: We gather the individual sheep into one big GREG flock to see the AGGREGate number.
mnemonic.story_zh: 我們把落單的羊集合成一群（GREG），就能算出「總計（AGGREGATE）」的數量。

example: The company's aggregate revenue from all international subsidiaries exceeded one billion dollars.

definition: Though; even though; although (used to introduce a concessive clause or modifying phrase).

mnemonic.story_en: The phrase is an old combination of 'all be it', meaning 'even though it is true'.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這是由三個字 all + be + it 組合而成的古老連詞，字面意思就是「儘管是這樣」。

example: The project was a complete success, albeit a very expensive one for the small company.

definition: To distribute resources or duties for a particular purpose according to a specific plan.

mnemonic.story_en: The manager will LOC place each budget item into a specific file to ALLOCATE resources fairly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 經理把每筆預算放到特定的定位（LOC）上，以便「分配（ALLOCATE）」資源。

example: The government decided to allocate more funds to public schools in rural areas.

definition: To change or cause to change in character or composition, typically in a small but significant way.

mnemonic.story_en: 如果你 ALTER（改變）計畫，你就是選擇了 ALTER（另一個）選項。

example: The internet has fundamentally altered the way people communicate and conduct business.

definition: One of two or more available possibilities or choices.
definition_zh: 可供選擇的事物；替代方案

mnemonic.story_en: When Plan A fails, you look for the ALTER (other) path, which is your ALTERNATIVE.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當 A 計劃失敗時，你會尋找 ALTER（另一個）路徑，也就是你的「替代方案（ALTERNATIVE）」。

example: Solar power offers a clean alternative to fossil fuels for electricity generation.

definition: To examine methodically and in detail the constitution or structure of something, especially information, for explanations.

mnemonic.story_en: Scientists need to LYS untie and break down complex components to ANALYZE the chemical compound.
mnemonic.story_zh: 科學家必須把複雜的化學成分徹底解開（LYS）來，才能全面「分析（ANALYZE）」它。

example: We need to analyze the survey results carefully before deciding on our next marketing campaign.

definition: Occurring once every year; calculated over the period of one year.

mnemonic.story_en: An ANN year passes by, and the company hosts its expected ANNUAL conference.
mnemonic.story_zh: 每過了一年（ANN），公司就會舉辦其預期的「年度（ANNUAL）」大會。

example: The company’s annual report showed a significant increase in profits over the last twelve months.

definition: To regard something as probable; to expect or predict and prepare for it in advance.

mnemonic.story_en: A good chess player will ANTE before the opponent moves, CIP take note and ANTICIPATE the strategy.
mnemonic.story_zh: 好的棋手會在對手落子之前（ANTE）就捕捉到（CIP）其意圖，並「預期（ANTICIPATE）」其策略。

example: Economists anticipate that inflation rates will stabilize by the end of the next quarter.

definition: Clearly visible or understood; obvious; seeming real or true, but not necessarily so.

mnemonic.story_en: When a ship comes to PEAR appear on the horizon, its presence becomes APPARENT.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當船隻在海平線上出現（PEAR）時，它的存在就變得「顯而易見（APPARENT）」了。

example: It became increasingly apparent that the two countries were heading toward a trade war.

definition: A section of additional matter at the end of a book or document; also a small, blind pouch attached to the cecum in the human body.

mnemonic.story_en: An extra chart is left to PEND hang at the end of the book as an APPENDIX.
mnemonic.story_zh: 額外的圖表被懸掛（PEND）在書本的最後，作為「附錄（APPENDIX）」。

example: Detailed statistical charts and survey questions are included in Appendix A.

definition: To recognize the full worth of something; to be grateful for something; or to increase in value over time.

mnemonic.story_en: Investors buy assets that will gain PRETI value and APPRECIATE over the years.
mnemonic.story_zh: 投資者購買那些會隨著時間增加價值（PRETI）而「升值（APPRECIATE）」的資產。

example: We deepy appreciate your help during this difficult transition period for our team.

definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; or the act of speaking to someone or moving closer physically.

mnemonic.story_en: To solve a difficult riddle, you must take a new path and PROCH near it from a unique APPROACH.
mnemonic.story_zh: 為了解決難題，你必須走一條新路，從一個獨特的「方法/角度（APPROACH）」去靠近（PROCH）它。

example: The company needs a fresh scientific approach to modern waste management and recycling.

definition: Suitable or proper in the circumstances or for a particular purpose.

mnemonic.story_en: Wearing a formal suit is the PROPRI proper and APPROPRIATE choice for a job interview.
mnemonic.story_zh: 穿著正式西裝是求職面試時最合適（PROPRI）且「恰當的（APPROPRIATE）」選擇。

example: It is not appropriate to use casual slang when writing a formal academic research paper.

definition: Close to the actual, but not completely accurate or exact.

mnemonic.story_en: Though not exact, the PROXIM near estimation gives us an APPROXIMATE budget for the trip.
mnemonic.story_zh: 雖然不完全精確，但最接近（PROXIM）的估算給了我們這次旅行的「大約（APPROXIMATE）」預算。

example: The approximate cost of the building repairs will be around five thousand dollars.

definition: A particular part or feature of something; or a specific way in which an idea or problem can be considered.

mnemonic.story_en: You must SPEC look at every angle to understand every ASPECT of the crisis.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你必須觀察（SPEC）每一個角度，才能理解這場危機的每一個「方面/層面（ASPECT）」。

example: Climate change is complex because it affects every aspect of human life, from economy to health.

definition: To bring together into one place for a common purpose; or to fit together the separate parts of an object.

mnemonic.story_en: The workers will meet SEMBL together in the factory to ASSEMBLE the new car parts.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工人們在工廠聚集在一起（SEMBL），藉此「組裝（ASSEMBLE）」新的汽車零件。

example: A large crowd began to assemble in the public square to protest the new tax policy.

definition: To evaluate or estimate the nature, ability, value, or quality of something.

mnemonic.story_en: The judges SESS sit at the long table to ASSESS the performance of each candidate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 評審們坐（SESS）在長桌旁，為了「評估（ASSESS）」每位候選人的表現。

example: Damages from the earthquake were assessed at over ten million dollars.

definition: To allocate a task, duty, or responsibility to someone; or to appoint someone to a specific job or role.

mnemonic.story_en: The teacher will SIGN mark each task with a name to ASSIGN homework to the students.
mnemonic.story_zh: 老師在每項任務上做記號（SIGN）寫下名字，以便向學生「指派（ASSIGN）」作業。

example: The manager decided to assign the most complex coding task to the senior engineer.

definition: To help someone, typically by doing a share of the work or providing technical or physical support.

mnemonic.story_en: A loyal helper will SIST stand by your side to ASSIST you with the heavy lifting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 忠實的助手會站（SIST）在你的身旁，來「協助（ASSIST）」你搬動重物。

example: The federal government offered to assist local police forces in investigating the cyberattack.

definition: To suppose to be the case, without proof; or to take on a responsibility, role, or debt officially.
definition_zh: 假定；假定；承擔（責任、角色）

mnemonic.story_en: Upon the CEO’s resignation, the vice president will SUME take control and ASSUME the leadership role.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在執行長辭職後，副總裁將拿取（SUME）主導權並「承擔（ASSUME）」領導角色。

example: We cannot assume that the store will be open on Christmas Day without checking their website.

definition: To tell someone something positively or confidently to dispel any doubts they may have.

mnemonic.story_en: The captain used a calm voice to make passengers feel SUR secure and ASSURE them the plane was safe.
mnemonic.story_zh: 機長用平靜的聲音讓乘客感到安全（SUR），向他們「保證（ASSURE）」飛機是安全的。

example: The doctor tried to assure the anxious parents that their child would make a full recovery.

definition: To fasten, join, or connect one object to another; or to attribute importance or value to something.
definition_zh: 附上；連結；使依戀；賦予（重要性）

mnemonic.story_en: Use a heavy TAC stake to bind and ATTACH the tent tightly to the ground.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用一個重的固定樁（TAC）來把帳篷牢牢「連結/附著（ATTACH）」在地面上。

example: Please remember to attach a copy of your resume to the email before submitting the application.

definition: To succeed in achieving a specific goal, status, or standard, especially after a long and hard effort.

mnemonic.story_en: The athlete ran fast to TAIN touch the finish line and ATTAIN the gold medal.
mnemonic.story_zh: 運動員奮力奔跑去觸碰（TAIN）終點線，藉此「獲得（ATTAIN）」金牌。

example: After ten years of grueling research, the scientist finally managed to attain academic recognition.

definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling about someone or something, typically one that is reflected in a person's behavior.

mnemonic.story_en: Your internal ATT fitness or mental posture determines your positive ATTITUDE toward challenges.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你內在心靈的姿態（ATT）決定了你面對挑戰時是否能展現出積極的「態度（ATTITUDE）」。

example: A positive attitude is often single-handedly responsible for career success and mental well-being.

definition: A writer of a book, article, or document; or the originator or creator of any plan or idea.

mnemonic.story_en: An AUT creator uses imagination to write a book and becomes its official AUTHOR.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個創造者（AUT）運用想像力寫出了一本書，進而成為了這本書的「作者（AUTHOR）」延續其思想。

example: The author of the controversial study refused to comment on the criticism from peers.

definition: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience; or a person with extensive knowledge in a field.
definition_zh: 權力；官方當局；權威專家

mnemonic.story_en: The founder has the AUT creative rights, giving him absolute AUTHORITY over company decisions.
mnemonic.story_zh: 創始者具有源初創造（AUT）的權利，這使他對公司決策擁有了絕對的「權力/權威（AUTHORITY）」。

example: Only the local housing authority has the legal power to approve construction in this historic zone.

definition: To convert a process or facility to be operated by automatic equipment or machines, reducing human labor.

mnemonic.story_en: The factory introduced advanced robots to AUTO self-run and AUTOMATE the manufacturing line.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工廠引進先進機器人使其能自我（AUTO）運作，從而將製造流程「自動化（AUTOMATE）」。

example: Our goal next year is to automate the billing system to save hundreds of administrative hours.

definition: Able to be used or obtained; at anyone's disposal; or free to do something or meet someone.
definition_zh: 可得到的；可利用的；有空的

mnemonic.story_en: When a tool has practical VAL value and is ready for use, it is AVAILABLE for workers.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當一個工具具有實用價值（VAL）且準備妥當，它對工人來說就是「可利用的（AVAILABLE）」的。

example: The customer service representative is available twenty-four hours a day to answer queries.

definition: An advantage or profit gained from something; or a payment made by the state or insurance company.

mnemonic.story_en: A generous program is designed to BENE do good and bring BENEFIT to poor families.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個慷慨的計畫被設計用來做（FIT）好（BENE）事，為貧困家庭帶來「好處/利益（BENEFIT）」。

example: Regular cardiovascular exercise provides long-term health benefits for the human body.

definition: A disproportionate weight in favor of or against an idea or thing, usually in a way that is closed-minded or unfair.

mnemonic.story_en: Instead of staying straight and neutral, the judge’s opinion showed a heavy BIAS slant toward one party.
mnemonic.story_zh: 法官的心思沒有保持公正筆直，而是歪斜（BIAS）向其中一方，展現出了「偏見（BIAS）」。

example: The media was heavily criticized for showing a clear political bias during the presidential election.

definition: Of short duration; not lasting for a long time; or using few words to explain something.

mnemonic.story_en: The manager gave a BRIEF explanation because time was very BREV short before the plane left.
mnemonic.story_zh: 經理做了一個「簡短的（BRIEF）」解釋，因為在飛機起飛前時間非常短暫（BREV）。

example: The president made a brief statement to the press before leaving for the summit.

definition: The mass or magnitude of something large; or the greater part / majority of something.
definition_zh: 體積；巨大群體；主要部分；大部分

mnemonic.story_en: The cargo ship carried heavy grains, and the BULK of its weight was stored safely in the bottom compartment.
mnemonic.story_zh: 貨船載著沉重的穀物，其重量的「主要部分（BULK）」都安全地儲存在底艙中。

example: The bulk of the company’s budget is spent on research and digital product development.

definition: Having the ability, fitness, or necessary skills to do something successfully.

mnemonic.story_en: A CAPable manager has the capacity to CAP hold complex details and lead a large team effectively.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個「有能力的（CAPABLE）」經理，有空間去容納（CAP）和掌控複雜的細節並有效帶領團隊。

example: She is a highly capable attorney who has won several difficult corporate legal battles.

definition: The maximum amount that something can contain; or the total intellectual or physical ability of a person.
definition_zh: 容量；能力；生產力；職位角色

mnemonic.story_en: The fuel tank has a huge CAP capacity, allowing it to CAP hold up to fifty gallons of oil.
mnemonic.story_zh: 油箱具有巨大的「容量（CAPACITY）」，使它能夠裝下（CAP）多達五十加侖的汽油。

example: The stadium was filled to capacity, with over eighty thousand excited soccer fans in attendance.
